candidates.attacker_control: The public `Configuration#addMapping(InputStream)` API accepts an arbitrary XML stream and stores it for later parsing; an application that feeds an uploaded/request-supplied mapping or validation descriptor to Hibernate Validator gives the attacker full control of the XML, including DOCTYPE declarations and entity references. For `META-INF/validation.xml`, control requires attacker influence over classpath/deployment resources rather than ordinary request data.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: XSD schema validation does exist, but it occurs after the first StAX parse/version probe and cannot prevent all external-entity resolution. `CloseIgnoringInputStream` only suppresses stream closes and does not secure parsing. Searches found no `SUPPORT_DTD`, `IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES`, `FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING`, or `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_*` configuration anywhere in the snapshot. The built-in `validation.xml` path is normally classpath-controlled, so the practical attack requires the application to expose or pass untrusted XML; some StAX providers or containers may harden or disable external entities by default. No runtime test or dependency-bytecode inspection was performed.
candidates.impact: A crafted descriptor can cause the server-side XML parser to fetch attacker-chosen URLs (SSRF to internal services) or read local files through external entities. Entity expansion can also consume CPU/memory for denial of service; file content may be disclosed through parser errors, logging, or downstream use of expanded values. The confidentiality and availability impact depends on the application's handling of the resulting parse error/value.
candidates.prerequisites: An application must build a ValidatorFactory using an attacker-controlled constraint-mapping stream (or otherwise make an untrusted XML descriptor reach the parser), and the selected StAX implementation must retain the JAXP defaults of DTD support and external-entity resolution. No JVM-level parser restrictions or custom hardened `XMLInputFactory` are configured in this snapshot.
candidates.root_cause: `XmlParserHelper` initializes `XMLInputFactory.newInstance()` with implementation defaults and calls `createXMLEventReader` on XML streams used for `META-INF/validation.xml` and caller-added constraint mappings, without setting `XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD` or `IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES` to false. Default JAXP StAX behavior permits DTDs and external entity resolution. The schema-version probe consumes the document prolog/root before XSD validation, so the later schema validation is not a control preventing entity resolution.
candidates.title: XML External Entity processing in Hibernate Validator XML descriptor parser
candidates.trace: `ConfigurationImpl.addMapping(InputStream)` stores the stream in `ValidationBootstrapParameters`; `ValidatorFactoryImpl` creates `XmlMetaDataProvider`, which calls `MappingXmlParser.parse`; `MappingXmlParser` calls `XmlParserHelper.createXmlEventReader` on the stream, then `getSchemaVersion` consumes events up to the root element before schema validation. `ValidationXmlParser` follows the same path for `validation.xml`. External DTDs/general entities referenced from the prolog or reachable schema-valid content are therefore resolved by `XMLInputFactory.createXMLEventReader`; later `Validator.validate` and the second parse create additional exposure points.
candidates.unverified: The source shows missing parser hardening, but actual external-entity resolution was not runtime-confirmed. I did not verify the default behavior of every StAX provider/container used with Hibernate Validator, the precise application-level path that supplies untrusted XML, or a concrete file-disclosure/SSRF response path. Tests and the referenced XML parser implementation are not present in the visible snapshot.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

coverage_summary: The assigned snapshot exposes 844 model-visible files with no over-5-MiB, sensitive-name, or symlink exclusions; no precomputed relation index was available. I inspected the engine XML parsing/configuration paths, constraint validators (including `SafeHtml`, `URL`, and email), message interpolation, CDI/configuration beans, and build/dependency metadata via text search and bounded reads. I did not read all 844 files line-by-line, and test sources and external dependency bytecode were not available in the visible snapshot (`engine/src/test` and `documentation/src` were empty), so dynamic behavior and third-party sanitizer/parser behavior remain uninspected.
limitations: No code, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were executed; the finding is source-level only.
The XML parser implementation and its default external-entity behavior depend on the runtime/container and were not verified.
The exact application endpoint or configuration that passes attacker-controlled XML to `Configuration#addMapping(InputStream)` is outside this repository and was not confirmed.
The XSD validation and second parse path may affect exploitability or error behavior in ways that require runtime confirmation.
Test sources and third-party dependency source (jsoup, StAX implementation) were not present in the visible snapshot.
Only the single strongest candidate was submitted per the review limit; the rejected leads remain unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.reason: `RegexpURLValidator` is an optional validator selected explicitly via constraint mapping, not the default `@URL` validator, and I did not establish a catastrophic backtracking path. `DomainNameUtil` uses possessive `++` quantifiers and appears structurally deterministic for the inspected patterns. This was not selected over the XXE lead.

The dependency version is old, but no concrete source-level bypass was identified in `SafeHtmlValidator`; the source uses jsoup's `Cleaner.isValid` and the actual sanitizer behavior is in an external dependency not inspected. This is a lead only, not a source-supported finding.

EL and script expressions come from application/annotation or mapping metadata, not from ordinary validated values by default. No attacker-controlled template path was traced; treating this as a vulnerability would require an unproven application misuse condition.

rejected_leads.lead: Arbitrary class loading/instantiation from untrusted constraint-mapping XML
rejected_leads.reason: This shares the untrusted-mapping configuration boundary with the XXE candidate but was not shown to be a distinct library vulnerability; it would require a classpath class with dangerous construction side effects. It was not submitted as a separate candidate.

summary: Reviewed the 844-file source snapshot as an untrusted-input source review. The strongest source-supported lead is missing XXE hardening in the XML descriptor path. Hibernate Validator's `XmlParserHelper` creates a default `XMLInputFactory` and parses `validation.xml` and caller-supplied constraint-mapping streams without disabling DTD support or external entities. Because the initial StAX parse (including the schema-version probe) occurs before XSD validation, a malicious mapping/validation descriptor can cause external entity or external-DTD resolution. I did not find a confirmed runtime exploit or a more direct remote path; other validator/interpolation leads were unconfirmed and are listed as rejected.
